_comment: Where the two bundled catalogs came from, pinned by CatalogTest
(FR-49, docs/design/20-local-spells-and-attacks.md decision 7). Every field below is a
statement of fact about a retrieval, not a claim anybody may edit to make a test pass: the
tests assert the counts and the spot-checks, and this file is the record they are checked
against. Re-fetching means re-recording, with a new commit and a new retrieval date.
READ contentLicence BEFORE reading sourceLicence: the two are about different things. The
game text is Wizards of the Coast's and is licensed by them; the JSON structuring came from
a community repository that licenses its own work separately.
LICENCE RULING (architect, 2026-09-12, review of FR-49): CC-BY-4.0 is accepted as the
content licence the bundled SRD text is carried under. Wizards of the Coast publish SRD 5.1
and SRD 5.2.1 under CC-BY-4.0; the intermediate repository's MIT/OGL note describes its own
code and is not the content licence. The attribution strings below are therefore the ones
the app prints, verbatim, and each carries the licence URL and the CC-BY-4.0 3(a)(1)
statement that the material has been modified. This closes the open item the build handover

spells.contentSource: System Reference Document 5.1, Wizards of the Coast LLC
spells.attribution: This work includes material from the System Reference Document 5.1 ("SRD 5.1") by Wizards of the Coast LLC, available under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License at https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode. The material has been modified for use in this app: it is reformatted as data and reduced to the fields the app displays.
spells.sourceLicence: MIT (the repository's own LICENSE.md), with the README stating of the game material: "The underlying material is released using the Open Gaming License Version 1.0a". The repository declares no CC-BY-4.0 notice and carries no attribution sentence of its own.
spells.editionNote: SRD 5.2.1 spells were sought first and do not exist in this repository. At commit 0b171af the whole of src/2024/en is: Ability-Scores, Alignments, Backgrounds, Classes, Conditions, Damage-Types, Equipment-Categories, Equipment, Feats, Features, Languages, Levels, Magic-Items, Magic-Schools, Monsters, Poisons, Proficiencies, Skills, Species, Subclasses, Subspecies, Traits, Weapon-Mastery-Properties, Weapon-Properties — there is no spell file. Decision 7's recorded fallback therefore applies: the complete SRD 5.1 set is used, and no editions are mixed inside this file.
spells.derivationNote: Every description, higher-level paragraph, name, school, casting time, range, duration and component string is the source's own text, verbatim — including its capitalisation and trailing full stops inside a material component, which are not normalised. components is assembled as the component letters joined with ", " plus the material in parentheses; nothing else is composed.

weapons.contentSource: System Reference Document 5.2.1, Wizards of the Coast LLC
weapons.attribution: This work includes material from the System Reference Document 5.2.1 ("SRD 5.2.1") by Wizards of the Coast LLC, available under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License at https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode. The material has been modified for use in this app: it is reformatted as data and reduced to the fields the app displays.
weapons.sourceLicence: MIT (the repository's own LICENSE.md). Its README's blanket OGL 1.0a note cannot describe this file's content: the 2024 SRD was published by Wizards of the Coast under CC-BY-4.0 only and has no Open Gaming Licence option, so the CC-BY-4.0 attribution above is the licence this material is carried under.
weapons.editionNote: The 2024 set is used because weapon mastery is a 2024 property and FR-47's badge path is what renders it — all 38 weapons carry a non-null mastery. This is a different edition from spells.json, recorded here rather than blended: no editions are mixed inside either file.
weapons.derivationNote: Names, damage dice, damage types, property names and mastery words are the source's own, verbatim. Three things are composed, from the source's own numbers and from nothing else: category, from the equipment-category indices ("Simple Melee", "Martial Ranged", …); damage, as "<dice> <type>" with a versatile weapon's two-handed die second ("1d8 / 1d10 slashing"); and the property parentheticals — Versatile (1d10), Thrown (Range 20/60), Ammunition (Range 80/320; Arrows) — which the 2024 source carries as structured two_handed_damage / throw_range / range / ammunition fields rather than as formatted strings. One source field has no slot in this schema and is therefore absent: the Lance's note "Two-handed unless mounted".
